Rashi on Menachot 88a:1:1.english: Which shall I bring in its place: To complete the tally of seven measuring vessels.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:2:1.english: And it is possible to measure with a half-log - Three half-logs in the morning and three in the evening.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:3:1.english: And it is possible to measure with a quarter-log - For four quarter-logs equal one log.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:3:2.hebrew: אלא - לפיכך לא היה משער לחביתין בשלשה חצאי לוג, ולא לחצי ברביעית, דזה הכלל היה במקדש וכו', ור' אלעזר בר ר' צדוק לית ליה זה הכלל:
Rashi on Menachot 88a:3:2.english: Rather - Therefore he would not measure [the oil] for the griddle-cakes by [repeatedly filling] a half-log [vessel] three times, nor [measure] a half-log by [repeatedly filling] a quarter-log [vessel], for this was the principle in the Temple, etc. [that a vessel used for measuring one quantity was not used for measuring another]. And Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, does not hold by this principle [since he maintains that the hin vessel had markings for several different measures].

Rashi on Menachot 88a:5:1.hebrew: בירוצי המדות - דכשממלאים את הכלי ביותר, נופל מן המשקה שבתוכו לדופני הכלי אילך ואילך, וכשמערין אותו מהרה לתוך כלי אחר, נופל המשקה בתוכו, ואם לאו, נופל לארץ:
Rashi on Menachot 88a:5:1.english: The overflow of the measures - For when they fill the vessel to excess, some of the liquid inside it falls onto the walls of the vessel, here and there; and when they pour it out quickly into another vessel, that liquid falls into it, but if not, it falls to the ground.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:5:2.hebrew: איכא בינייהו - לר' יהודה דאמר מלמטה למעלה, קסבר בירוצי המדות נתקדשו. כיצד? דרביעית יהיב ליה רחמנא למשה מסיני, ואמר ליה: שער ברביעית את האחרים, וימדוד שני רביעית ויעשה מהם חצי לוג, ושוב לוג וכו' עד הין, ושער אותו הין כ"כ גדול שיכנסו בירוצין של כל אלו מדות, דבירוצין נתקדשו. וכשאדם מערה שני כלים קטנים בכלי המחזיק שניהם, יכול לשופכו לאלתר כולו בגדול עם הבירוצין, וכן השני. הלכך צריך הגדול המקבל שניהם להיות גדול כל כך שיקבל אותם ואת בירוציהם, הילכך נתקדשו:
Rashi on Menachot 88a:5:2.english: There is [a difference] between them - According to Rabbi Yehuda, who says [the vessels are listed] from smaller to larger, he holds that the overflow of the measuring vessels was consecrated. How so? The Merciful One gave Moses at Sinai [a vessel of] a quarter-log, and told him: Calculate the other [vessels] using the quarter-log - measure out two quarter-logs and make from them a half-log, and then continue likewise up to a log, and so on until the hin. And He sized that hin to be so large that the overflow of all these measures would fit into it, for it is through the overflow that they became consecrated. For when a person pours [the contents of] two small vessels into a vessel that holds them both, he can pour it all at once into the larger vessel together with the overflow, and likewise for the second [vessel]. Therefore the large vessel that receives both of them must be big enough to receive them together with their overflow; hence they were consecrated.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:7:1.hebrew: והין יהיב ליה רחמנא למשה, ואמר ליה שער ממנו את האחרים: חצי ההין, ושלישית ההין, ורביעית ההין. וכיון דצריך לשפוך ממדה גדולה לחלקם לשני כלים, אין יכול לשפוך בבת אחת עם הבירוצים, לפי שזה כלי גדול וזה כלי קטן, וצריך לשפוך על יד. ומתוך שממעטין, נחסרין הבירוצין מה שצף על הכלי כל שעה, ולא היו שם בירוצין. והיינו דנפקי בירוצין, וכיון דלא הוו התם בירוצין, לא נתקדשו:
Rashi on Menachot 88a:7:1.english: And according to the one who says [the vessels are listed] from top to bottom, he holds that the overflow of the measures was not consecrated - The Merciful One gave him [Moses] the hin, and told him: From it, calibrate the others - half the hin, a third of the hin, and a quarter of the hin. And since he must pour from the large measure to divide it between two vessels, he cannot pour it all at once together with the overflow, because one is a large vessel and the other a small vessel, and he must pour it out little by little. And since they pour small amounts at a time, the overflow - what floats over the vessel each time - is reduced, so there was no overflow there. And this is [the meaning of] "the overflow goes out." And since there was no overflow there, they were not consecrated.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:8:1.english: There is room to say [the leftover] became consecrated, and there is room to say it did not become consecrated, etc.: As we explain there.

Rashi on Menachot 88a:8:2.hebrew: במלאים קמיפלגי - דכתיב (במדבר ז׳:י״ג) שניהם מלאים סלת, וה"ה בשאר כלי [לח]. מאן דאמר ממעלה למטה קסבר מלאים דווקא, דהאי קרא במזרק שהוא כלי לח, שלא יחסר ולא יותיר. אלא ההין מחלק בתוך שני חצאי ההין מצומצמים, וכן כולם:
Rashi on Menachot 88a:8:2.english: They disagree about [the meaning of] "full" - As it is written (Numbers 7:13): "both of them full of fine flour" - and the same applies to other liquid vessels. The one who says [the order proceeds] from the largest to the smallest holds that "full" means precisely [the exact amount] - for this verse is stated with regard to the basin, which is a liquid vessel - that it should hold neither less nor more. Rather, [this is achieved in that] the hin is divided into two exactly equal halves, and so for all the rest.

Tosafot on Menachot 88a:3:1.hebrew: אף לדבריכם חצי לוג [ולוג] לא יעשה שרביעית היתה שם - ורבנן סברי דלא דמי כמדה של לוג ומחצה, לא צריכה אלא לחביתין, אבל חצי לוג צריך למילי טובא: לסוטה, ולתודה, ולמנורה:
Tosafot on Menachot 88a:3:1.english: Even according to your view, a half-log [and a log] would not work, since a quarter-log was there - The Rabbis hold that this is not comparable to a measure of a log-and-a-half: such a measure would be needed only for the griddle-cakes, whereas a half-log is needed for many things - for the sotah, for the thanks-offering, and for the candelabrum.

Tosafot on Menachot 88a:6:1.hebrew: בירוצי מדות נתקדשו - למאן דאמר לא נתקדשו, ניחא הא דאמר לקמן (מנחות דף צ.): מותר נסכים לקיץ מזבח. ומפרש רבינו חיים בר ר' יוסי, בירוצי מדות, דיש להן פדיון, ולוקחין ממותר נסכים כבשים לעולה, ומקיצין אותו. אבל למאן דאמר נתקדשו, קשיא הא אין להם פדיון. ויש לומר דמיירי בנסכי צבור, ולב בית דין מתנה עליהן, כדמפ' בירושלמי דשקלים. ומיהו אם לנו מיפסלי בלינה, כדאמרינן לקמן, דלענין הכי לא מתנו. ומדמיפסלי בלינה נמי, יש לדקדק דקסבר בירוצי מדות נתקדשו. ואם תאמר: ונגזור שמא יאמרו מוציאין מכלי שרת לחול, כדגזרינן התם לר' יוסי בלח בדנעקר, ולעיל בפ' התודה (מנחות דף עט:)? ויש לומר דהכא לא גזרינן, דאמרינן לנפשייהו: בירוצין לא נתקדשו:
Tosafot on Menachot 88a:6:1.english: The overflow of the measuring vessels became consecrated - According to the one who says it did not become consecrated, this fits well with what is stated further on (Menachot 90a): "the leftover of the libations goes to the 'dessert offering' of the altar." Rabbeinu Chaim bar R' Yosi explains that this leftover from the measuring vessels has redemption, and that with the leftover of the libations they purchase lambs for a burnt-offering, thereby providing the altar with its "dessert." But according to the one who says it did become consecrated, this is difficult, since such [consecrated] items have no redemption. One can answer that [that passage] is speaking of communal libations, for which the court makes an [implicit] mental stipulation, as is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim. However, if such an item remains overnight, it is disqualified through the law of "lodging overnight" (linah), as is stated further on - for in that respect, no such stipulation was made. And indeed, from the fact that it is disqualified through lodging overnight, one can also deduce that [the author of this ruling] holds that the overflow of the measuring vessels did become consecrated. And if you will say: let us then decree [a prohibition] out of concern that people will conclude that one may remove an item from a sacred vessel for secular use - just as we find such a decree stated elsewhere, in the name of R' Yosi, regarding liquid that had been poured out [of its vessel], and above in the chapter "HaTodah" (Menachot 79b) - one may answer that here we do not make such a decree, for [in this case] we reason among ourselves that the overflow was never consecrated to begin with.
